decisions.statement: A landing starts only where it holds the turn.
Eight gigabytes available is the least a landing starts on.
What is available is what the kernel says, rather than what is unused.
A landing the workstation has no room for waits rather than refusing.
A turn is taken under a lock, so two landings never read the same free memory.
A turn is held only while it is taken, so a run that died holding one stops nothing.
A least read from the environment is used in place of the least stated here.
Nothing here counts what memory a landing is about to take.
One landing is spaced from the next by what memory is free rather than by a wait.

definition: the turn a landing waits for, and the memory the workstation keeps free to give it
